sentences.text: The known remains consist of a single specimen that preserves most of the skull and the tip of the fourth wing finger.
This skull is narrow from side to side but very tall, featuring an enormous external nostril that serves as the largest cranial opening.
The skull roof displays a midline crest and large crests along the upper temporal edges, which marked the attachment points for jaw-closing muscles.
A prominent bump at the rear of the skull, known as the nuchal crest, indicates that large neck muscles were housed in that area.

The unflattened braincase allowed scientists to create the first endocranial reconstruction of a Triassic pterosaur, revealing a brain with large cerebral lobes, bulging optic lobes, and small olfactory lobes.
The lower front of the jaw possesses a keel, and the entire jaw is hollow and likely filled with air, featuring large pneumatic openings at the rear.
This animal is the sole example of a non-pterodactyloid pterosaur living in a desert area and is 65 million years older than other pterosaurs that lived in arid zones.
Its teeth are heterodont, possessing three distinct types: long tusk-like teeth, leaf-shaped teeth, and small blades.
Behind the tusks lies a toothless gap followed by thirty-eight tiny teeth on each side of the jaw.
Fossils were recovered from the Saints & Sinners Quarry located in northeastern Utah.
The fossil site was discovered in 2007 by Dan Chure and George Engelmann while studying the Nugget Sandstone.
The discovery of this genus was reported in scientific literature in 2015.
Caelestiventus shows that early pterosaurs were morphologically and ecologically diverse and that the Dimorphodontidae originated in the Triassic period.
The two elongated tusks were located near the front of each side of the jaw and possibly opposed similar teeth at the tip of the snout in the premaxilla.
Each upper jaw in the skull is armed with twelve large triangular leaf-shaped teeth, reinforced on both sides by a central crest and ending in two points.
Caelestiventus belongs to the family Dimorphodontidae.

Phylogenetic analyses show that Caelestiventus is the sister taxon of Dimorphodon macronyx within the family Dimorphodontidae, defined by Britt and colleagues as the least inclusive clade containing Caelestiventus hanseni and Dimorphodon macronyx.
Caelestiventus lived from the Carnian to the Toarcian stages, between 237 and 174.7 million years ago.
Only one fossil occurrence of Caelestiventus has been recorded.

Besides Caelestiventus, the Saints & Sinners Quarry has produced a diverse vertebrate fauna including two genera of sphenosuchians, two genera of sphenodonts, a drepanosaurid, a procolophonid, and two theropod dinosaurs – a coelophysoid and a medium-sized genus represented only by teeth.
